nodes.summary: The generator commutes with the transition function.
nodes.title: Generator commutes with the transition function

nodes.summary: The semigroup property (Chapman–Kolmogorov equation): `P (s + t) = P s * P t`.
nodes.title: Chapman–Kolmogorov equation for the transition semigroup

nodes.summary: For every real `c`, `exp (t • Q) = e^{-c t} • exp (t • (Q + c • 1))` (Jensen 1953).
nodes.title: Uniformization

nodes.summary: The transition function of a rate matrix is row-stochastic for `t ≥ 0` (Norris 1997, Theorem 2.1.2).
nodes.title: Transition function of a rate matrix is row-stochastic

nodes.summary: If `Q` annihilates the constant vector `1`, then `P t` fixes it: `P t *ᵥ 1 = 1`.
nodes.title: Transition function fixes the constant vector

nodes.summary: If `A` has nonnegative entries, so does `exp (t • A)` for `t ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Exponential of a nonnegative matrix is nonnegative

nodes.summary: The transition function of a rate matrix has nonnegative entries for `t ≥ 0`, by uniformization.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the transition function of a rate matrix

nodes.summary: Rescaling the generator rescales time: `exp (t • (a • Q)) = exp ((a * t) • Q)`.
nodes.title: Rescaling the generator rescales time

nodes.summary: At time `0` the transition function is the identity.
nodes.title: Transition function at time zero is the identity

nodes.summary: The transition function `P t = exp (t • Q)` of the finite continuous-time Markov chain with generator `Q` (Norris 1997, Theorem 2.1.1).
nodes.title: Transition semigroup of a continuous-time Markov chain

nodes.summary: The Kolmogorov backward equation `P' t = Q * P t` (Norris 1997, Theorem 2.1.1).
nodes.title: Kolmogorov backward equation

nodes.summary: The Kolmogorov forward equation `P' t = P t * Q` (Norris 1997, Theorem 2.1.1).
nodes.title: Kolmogorov forward equation

nodes.summary: The rows of the transition function of a rate matrix sum to `1`, for every real `t`.
nodes.title: Rows of the transition function sum to one

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
